ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, general partners, limited partners, UBOs and authorized signatories against UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, Canada's Special Economic Measures Act schedules, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act lists, and provincial no-go lists. All individuals with 25% or more ownership or control and all senior management undergo politically exposed person (PEP) identification using enhanced due diligence; source of wealth and source of funds are verified in every case. Continuous adverse-media monitoring and re-screening are required before each significant disbursement and at least annually. This manufacturing operation is not automatically a FINTRAC reporting entity under the PCMLTFA, but the corporate general partner or investor may be an MSB if it processes third-party funds; prudent practice and payment-rail contractual requirements (e.g., Stripe/platform) require full KYC/CDD and PEP/sanctions screening regardless of statutory exemption.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name clearance and reservation portal (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, every enterprise name registered in Quebec must have a French version; the French form governs. For a limited partnership, the legal ending must be 'société en commandite' or its abbreviation 'S.E.C.' A foreign brand or trademark may be transliterated only where no acceptable French lexical form exists, and the French generic component must remain predominant. Punctuation, apostrophes, diacritics and numerals must follow the Registrar's orthographic rules; acronyms and initials are accepted but cannot be used as a substitute for the French legal ending.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving a name-refusal notice, the applicant must file a written demande de révision with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. The application must identify the refused name, the statutory ground for refusal, any corrected form of the name, and all supporting documents, including the original name-analysis receipt and trademark evidence if relevant. The Registrar must issue a decision within 60 days of receipt. A further judicial review lies before the Court of Québec or, where a federal legal issue arises, the Superior Court of Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A new name-reservation application may be filed simultaneously while preserving priority, subject to payment of a new statutory fee; no refund is granted on refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be accepted for correspondence, mailing address and service of process, but it cannot satisfy the Quebec statutory requirement that the limited partnership maintain an establishment (établissement) in Quebec for the purpose of legal publicity and taxation. Because the proposed business scope is ISIC 3250 medical/dental instrument manufacturing — specifically the thermoforming and automated trimming of multilayer clear-aligner sheets — a physical production facility, warehouse or industrial workspace in Quebec is mandatory for commercial substance, health and safety compliance, and municipal licensing. The virtual office is only a supplementary administrative address and does not support substantive manufacturing activity or regulatory inspections.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-High (65–75% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months of operation). The quantified risk reflects mandatory oversight by CNESST (occupational health and safety), municipal fire-code and zoning officers, Revenu Québec substance-audit teams, and possibly Health Canada if a Medical Device Establishment Licence is triggered for aligner sheets classified as medical devices. The likelihood in the first year alone is approximately 40–50% because of the industrial machinery, electrical installations, and thermoforming/trimming processes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, Book 4 (CCQ, arts. 2236-2262) governing societes en commandite; An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 22-36 (declaration of registration); Part XVIII.1 and Schedule of fees of P-44.1; Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282 (Health Canada); Quebec Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar, REQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Declaration d'immatriculation) for a Limited Partnership (Societe en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Quebec limited partnership. Capital contributions are governed by the partnership agreement; no escrow account is required. Limited partners' liability is confined to the unpaid balance of their agreed contribution, provided they do not take part in the control or management of the enterprise (CCQ arts. 2247-2249). Contributions must be disclosed in the declaration of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner of the Limited Partnership: (1) approves the submission of the Declaration of Registration to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, designating the registered office at [Address], Montreal, Quebec; (2) subscribes and records the capital contributions of the general and limited partners as set out in the Partnership Agreement; (3) appoints [Name] as Manager of the Partnership, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each with authority to open bank accounts, sign contracts, and file statutory returns; and (4) authorizes any partner or officer to execute all ancillary documents and pay all fees required, including settlement of the registration and regulatory fees. The resolution is effective on signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Online Name Search and Declaration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a statutory name search through the REQ's central enterprise index and request a name declaration (declaration de nom) for the proposed firm name, e.g., '[Brand] Dental Aligners, S.E.C.' The name must comply with the naming rules prescribed by the Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Submit the name declaration online, pay the applicable fee, and obtain the REQ name attestation before filing the declaration of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ name declaration form
Preliminary NUANS search report
Copy of the general partner's government-issued identification
Mandate of the general partner appointing a representative, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or queried, amend the distinctive elements online to remove prohibited, misleading, or confusing expressions, or file a revised name declaration within 15 days. A written request for reconsideration may be submitted to the REQ legal publicity sector with a revised name proposal and supporting trademark or trade-name evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Partnership Agreement and Preparation of the Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or Quebec legal counsel; REQ electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the partnership agreement (contrat de societe) specifying the firm name, registered office address in Quebec, identity of the general partner, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, and term. Complete the REQ electronic Declaration of Registration form, disclosing the general partner and, where all general partners are legal persons, designating a natural person as the partners' agent (art. 35, P-44.1). Attach the required schedules and the name attestation.
required_dossiers: Executed Partnership Agreement
REQ electronic Declaration of Registration form
Consent of general partner to act as such
Proof of lease or ownership of the registered office in Quebec
Notarized mandate, if a representative is designated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any omission or inconsistency identified by REQ, such as missing date of birth, domicile, or contribution schedule, and resubmit the declaration. A Notice of Incomplete Application must be cured within the deadline stated in the notice; failure to cure may result in the application being treated as withdrawn, requiring a fresh filing with the applicable fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration and Issuance of the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Registration electronically at the REQ portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) and pay the CAD 37 electronic filing fee. Upon processing, the REQ issues the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and an attestation of registration. The limited partnership is validly constituted against third parties from the date of registration, subject to the publicity regime of P-44.1.
required_dossiers: Signed Declaration of Registration
Proof of payment of the registration fee
REQ name attestation
Designation of natural-person agent, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is objected to or refused, respond in writing to the REQ notice within 30 days, submitting corrected schedules or a rectifying declaration. Where the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Court of Quebec for an order directing registration, or submit a regularized declaration accompanied by a justification letter and the prescribed fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the federal Business Number (BN) through CRA's Business Registration Online service using the NEQ and partnership details. Register for GST/HST and, if applicable, the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) with Revenu Quebec. If the partnership will employ Quebec residents, register for source deductions, Quebec Pension Plan (QPP), and Quebec Parental Insurance Plan (QPIP). The limited partnership is a pass-through entity for income tax purposes and must file an information return (T5013) annually with CRA.
required_dossiers: Copy of the REQ attestation and NEQ
Executed Partnership Agreement
General partner's Canada Revenue Agency account or social insurance number
Physical location details of the partnership's establishment in Quebec
Banking confirmation of the partnership's capital account deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where CRA or Revenu Quebec issues a clarification request, provide the REQ certificate, the partnership agreement, and a legal opinion on pass-through status within the prescribed response period. If an account registration is delayed, operate under a pending status and respond to the agency's deficiency letter, requesting a retroactive effective date based on the REQ registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, Insurance, Annual Publicity, and Establishment Licence Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chartered bank; commercial insurer; REQ annual update; Health Canada - Medical Devices Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian business bank account in the partnership's name using the REQ attestation and the general partner's resolution. Secure commercial general liability, product liability, and general partner's errors and omissions insurance. File the required annual declaration (declaration de mise a jour) with REQ each year and, before placing dental clear aligners on the market, obtain a Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) from Health Canada under the Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation and NEQ
Resolution of the general partner authorizing the bank account
Executed Partnership Agreement
Identification documents of the general partner's authorized signatories
Proof of registered office address
Commercial insurance binder
Draft Quality Management System and Standard Operating Procedures for MDEL application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC queries, provide a Quebec legal opinion confirming the general partner's authority. If Health Canada issues a deficiency letter on the MDEL application, respond with corrected documentation within 60 days and resubmit the applicable fee. Annual REQ declarations may be corrected without penalty before the statutory deadline for limited partnerships.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada - Medical Devices Directorate; Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE) for industrial establishment confirmation; Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282; Quebec industrial establishment authorization (attestation de conformite) for thermoforming operations under the Environment Quality Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Quebec (MELCCFP) - Directorate of Industrial and Authorization Assessments
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Declaration of Compliance (attestation de conformite) under the Regulation respecting the application of the Environment Quality Act; a full EIA is not mandatory for a medium-capacity thermoplastic thermoforming plant, but a sectoral authorization or municipal industrial wastewater permit may apply depending on discharge volume and wastewater destination.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater must meet the limits of the city sewer by-law implementing the Regulation respecting industrial wastewater discharges (e.g., pH 6.0-9.5; total suspended solids not exceeding 300 mg/L; oil and grease not exceeding 15 mg/L; compliance with municipal heavy-metal thresholds). Process air emissions from thermoforming and trimming must remain below the VOC exposure and emission guidelines under the Clean Air Regulation (Chapter Q-2, r. 4.1) and Health Canada occupational exposure limits. All scrap PETG and PU materials must be managed under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials, with waste manifests retained for a minimum of 3 years.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certificate of conformity issued by the municipal fire service under the Quebec Construction Code (Chapter 1, Fire Safety); structural load certification for thermoforming and trimming equipment from a Quebec professional engineer (OIQ); CNESST occupational health and safety registration and first-aid clearance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (LSST); compliance with the Machine Safety Regulation for guards, emergency stops, and heat-surface protection on all thermoformers and trimmers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec provincial taxes, QST, and corporate tax administration; CRA Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec's Registraire des entreprises are the applicable portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) by registering through CRA's Business Registration Online or a paper RC1 form; simultaneously or subsequently register with Revenu Québec for a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), QST account, and provincial payroll and tax accounts. Registration requires legal entity proof, foreign registration documents, Canadian agent or place of business details, and appointment of a representative for tax purposes, with the BN granted immediately and provincial accounts linked thereafter.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: A limited partnership (LP) is not a separate taxable entity for Canadian income tax purposes; each partner is taxed on their allocated share of income, with limited partners having liability protection but no active participation in management, and non-resident partners are subject to Canadian withholding, Part XII.2 tax on specified partnership distributions, and income tax under Part X.3 or withholding on allocated income as applicable. Territorial scope: full Canadian and provincial tax nexus, with Quebec-specific QST registration where the LP carries on commercial activity in Quebec, unless the $30,000 threshold relief applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide check-the-box elections akin to the US; however, available elections include: (1) filing a designated partnership election under section 186 to treat a partner's share of certain income as business income; (2) electing under subsection 216.1 to treat non-resident partner's share of Canadian-source income as income from a business other than through a permanent establishment for treaty relief; (3) choosing to be a passive limited partner under subsection 34.2 to accelerate deductions; (4) making the partnership's taxation year election under subsection 34.1; and (5) electing under the hybrid mismatch rules in subsection 18.4, 18.5, and 18.6 to conform or adjust the tax treatment for foreign hybrid entities, ensuring no deductible foreign tax credit mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) at the federal level and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) at the provincial level, together forming a VAT-like consumption tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For GST/HST, the general threshold is CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide gross revenue from taxable supplies; for QST, the Quebec threshold is also CAD 30,000 of taxable turnover within Quebec, subject to mandatory registration once exceeded or for certain activities (e.g., non-residents carrying on commercial activity in Quebec may be required regardless of threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not impose a centralized real-time tax clearance or digital stamping mandate for invoices. B2B invoices issued by a GST/QST registrant must contain the registrant's BN and QST registration number; electronic invoices must be securely transmitted and preserved in a compatible audit trail. Filing is electronic via CRA's GST/HST NETFILE, My Business Account, and Revenu Québec's provincial online services, with specific API-enabled bulk filing available for large filers, but no immediate fiscal clearance before invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported from Canada by the LP to a non-resident for use outside Canada, provided title and risk pass outside Canada; services rendered to non-residents where the LP performs all or substantially all of the service at an address outside Canada; or optional zero-rating for certain toll conversion and freight services. Supplies of dental aligner sheets to export markets are zero-rated only upon documentation proving physical exportation, or direct contractual terms with a foreign orthodontic laboratory or clinic.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) or equivalent electronic export reporting through Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA))
Bill of Lading or airway waybill evidencing shipment to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank confirmation of receipt of foreign currency proceeds in the LP's or its authorized foreign exchange intermediary's account
Commercial invoice matching the exported goods' description, quantity, and value
Customs Officer's endorsed proof of departure where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec can, upon audit, re-classify zero-rated exports as taxable supplies if documentation is incomplete or the goods were not demonstrably exported. Penalties include: reassessment of GST/QST due plus interest from the settlement date; a 6% penalty under subsection 280(2) of the Excise Tax Act on numeric GST errors; gross negligence penalties of up to $5,000 or 10% of the tax sought, and 50% of unpaid tax for misstatements; and criminal prosecution for fraudulent export claims under section 327.1 of the Excise Tax Act, leading to fines up to CAD 100,000 or imprisonment up to 5 years. For QST, similar penalties apply under the Quebec Tax Administration Act, including a 50% penalty for false statements and seizure of refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential banking supervision by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime for both current and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange controls, no requirement for Bank of Canada approval on capital injections, and no restriction on profit remittances or dividend/distribution repatriation by a Quebec limited partnership to non-resident limited partners, provided the remittance is made through a regulated Canadian financial institution. Tax compliance obligations, including Part XIII withholding tax on distributions to non-resident partners and Quebec TP-1021 reporting, apply independently of FX rules. Large cross-border transfers exceeding CAD 10,000 or equivalent are reportable to FINTRAC, and any non-resident partner funding above applicable thresholds must be supported by source of funds documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable to Canada. There is no statutory export proceeds surrender rate or mandatory conversion timeline. Exporters retain 100% of foreign currency receipts and may hold them in foreign currency accounts with domestic chartered banks. However, FINTRAC electronic fund transfer reporting applies to any cross-border receipt of CAD 10,000 or more, and export documentation must be preserved for the Canada Revenue Agency and customs audits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low immediate viability for offshore digital EMIs. Foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not passportable into Canada; such entities cannot operate as banks and cannot directly provide CAD-denominated clearing. An offshore EMI may only provide ancillary services if it becomes a FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business (MSB), maintains a Canadian agent or physical presence, and complies with the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) once applications become mandatory. Due to the LP's bankability requirements, a Canadian Schedule I bank or Desjardins is the legally preferable treasury corridor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is generally not mandatory for a low-risk Quebec limited partnership opening an operational account with a major Schedule I bank. Remote onboarding is permitted using video identification, digital signatures, and electronic verification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners. However, if any general or limited partner is resident in a high-risk jurisdiction, is a politically exposed person, or the partnership fails to provide transparent ownership documentation, the bank may require an in-person director interview at a Canadian branch or a notarized identity verification package. For Quebec, the LP must be registered in the Registraire des entreprises and provide the registration declaration (déclaration d'immatriculation).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure of the limited partnership due to the absence of a public Quebec LP beneficial owner register
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original partnership agreement, register of partners, a detailed beneficial ownership chart identifying all individuals holding 10% or more of capital or control rights, certified passports, proof of residential address, and a signed attestation of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners in the partnership structure with limited or no tax-treaty protection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax residence certificate issued by the partner's jurisdiction, entity formation documents equivalent to EPC-compliant registration, payment of Quebec registration fees showing indicative commercial substance, and bank references from the foreign partner's account-holding institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No minimum statutory capital and potential risk of classification as a shell or conduit entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan showing thermoforming and automated trimming capacity, lease agreements for production facilities, vendor purchase orders, proforma invoices for dental aligner sheets, equipment lists, and projected cash-flow statements for the first three operating quarters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade inflows and outflows to jurisdictions with elevated money-laundering or sanctions risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanction screening results for the complete partner and counterparty chain, commercial sales contracts, bill of lading and airway bill evidence, Incoterms designations, customs entry documents, and letters of credit or bank payment undertakings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex allocation of profits and carried interest among partners creating unclear economic beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital account schedules, distributions waterfall analysis, general partner allocation calculations, audited or reviewed partnership financial statements, and a notarized resolution authorizing the account signatories and treasury managers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Incoming partner contributions and shareholder loans must be routed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the remitting bank to the Quebec LP's Canadian operational account. The payment instruction must include in field 70 an explicit purpose such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION /LP CASH IN' or, where accepted, the ISO 20022 purpose code 'CAPT' or 'CORP'. For CAD transfers within Canada, Payments Canada Lynx or Real-Time Rail may settle same-day retail payments; for USD transfers, the remitting institution should use CHIPS ABA or Fedwire. The receiving bank will require the partnership agreement, a resolution confirming the capital injection, source-of-funds declarations for each partner, and FINTRAC reporting if any component exceeds CAD 10,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for clear aligner sheet purchases and equipment imports should clear through SWIFT MT103 for direct payment obligations or through commercial letters of credit (MT700) for documentary trade. CAD payments settle via Payments Canada Lynx for high-value payments and Real-Time Rail for immediate lower-value payments; USD payments settle via Fedwire or CHIPS for same-day value. The issuing bank will require underlying contracts, marine/airway bills, inspection certificates, commercial invoices, and evidence of customs clearance for all cross-border goods shipments. Netting and intra-group interoperability should be handled in a centralized in-house bank ledger to minimize SWIFT fees.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR FX forwards up to 12 months executed with a licensed Schedule I bank treasury desk under ISDA/CSA documentation
FX swaps for temporary CAD/USD liquidity conversion while maintaining matched settlement dates
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD for reducing long-term interest rate and currency risk on partner capital loans
Over-the-counter FX options (call or put on CAD/USD) with a bank-approved counterparty credit limit

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for illiquid exotic currency pairs where physical CAD settlement is impossible; NDFs are non-standard for CAD because the Canadian dollar is an freely deliverable major currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Enterprise Registry Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for the société en commandite
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Ministère de la Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the anniversary of the LP's initial registration date per Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, s. 49
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 15 per month late filing penalty capped at CAD 150; continued default triggers a REQ notice and administrative strike-off (radiation) under P-44.1; attestation certificates suspended; false or omitted partner declarations engage civil liability of the general partner

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (Form T5013, Schedule 50 and partner allocation slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Sudbury Tax Centre (electronic filing via GFET)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership fiscal period end; December 31 year-end is due May 31 of the following calendar year (Income Tax Regulations, s. 229)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 30 per day penalty to a maximum of CAD 2,100; incomplete Schedule 50 or incorrect partner allocations trigger reassessments of partner returns and Part XIII withholding exposure on non-resident partners

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Partnership Information Return (Form CO-17 / CO-17.1 with Relevé 31 equivalents)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the fiscal period end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end); large partnerships with a corporate general partner are mandatorily required to file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties under the Tax Administration Act, CQLR c. A-6.002, mirroring CRA daily amounts up to CAD 2,100; formal demand can deny partner deductions and add interest and 5% penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) return for annual registrants (Form GST34 and Form FPZ-38)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST program) and Revenu Québec (QST)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for annual filers (March 31 for December 31 year-end); monthly or quarterly remittances apply when taxable revenues exceed CAD 1.5M
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% late filing penalty plus 1% per full month compounded up to 12 months on any balance due; daily interest accrues; Revenu Québec may add specific QST penalties and commence collection measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) annual renewal for the thermoforming and aligner manufacturing site
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Health Canada, Medical Devices Directorate, Market Authorization and Licensing Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal submitted before the December 31 annual expiry; a renewal filed before expiry maintains the licence in force (Medical Devices Regulations, SOR/98-282, ss. 46-50)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Import or sale without a valid MDEL halts customs release and distribution; violations of the Food and Drugs Act attract fines up to CAD 5,000,000 on indictment plus product seizure and stop-sale orders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory financial audit is imposed on a privately held Quebec LP by the Registraire des entreprises or Revenu Québec. A compulsory independent audit is triggered only if (i) the partnership agreement or lender covenants require it, (ii) the LP becomes a reporting issuer under the Quebec Securities Act, CQLR c. V-1.1, or (iii) CRA or Revenu Québec issues a formal audit demand. The ISO 13485 quality management system audit required under SOR/98-282 for the dental aligner plant is a compliance audit, not a financial statement audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable or large cross-border LPs; ASPE (Part II) is the default private enterprise framework accepted by CRA and Revenu Québec. Multi-layer aligner inventory and work-in-progress must be valued under ASPE 3031 / IAS 2 equivalent provisions; GAAP-basis partnership financials must reconcile with the tax allocation basis reported on T5013 and CO-17.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No dedicated annual UBO register is currently operational for Quebec LPs; the planned Registre des bénéficiaires ultimes under SQ 2021, c. 19 remains suspended. Ownership confirmation is achieved annually through (i) the REQ annual declaration listing every general and limited partner with name, address and nominal capital contribution, (ii) T5013 Schedule 50 and CO-17 reporting each partner's income and loss allocation percentage, and (iii) REQ modification declarations filed within 15 days of any partner admission, withdrawal or transfer. Omission or misstatement of a partner triggers REQ penalties and loss of legal publicity protection for the partnership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members - for the LP structure, the Register of Partners (limited and general) recording capital contributions, allocation percentages and transfer or admission history
Register of Directors - for the LP structure, the Register of General Partners (commandité) and mandated managers exercising management powers and custody of records
Minute Book - general partner and limited partner resolutions, annual minutes and written consents kept at the LP head office in Quebec

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 700 per year (CAD 350 - 950) for a Quebec head-office address, service of process agent and annual REQ compliance monitoring provided by a commercial agent or law firm
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,500 - 18,000 (CAD 9,000 - 24,000) for an independent audit of a private manufacturing LP with cross-border partners; reduced to USD 3,500 - 6,500 for a review engagement where no audit covenant exists

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined headline general corporate rate (15% federal + 11.5% Quebec provincial); for a Limited Partnership not qualifying as a specified qualified partnership under the Quebec Taxation Act, the LP is deemed a corporation for provincial purposes; for partners, income otherwise flows through to partners as a non-resident allocation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Manufacturing and processing (M&P) federal profit deduction of 13% (s.125.1), reducing the federal effective rate to roughly 13.05% on M&P profits; Quebec M&P deduction of 3.5% reduces provincial effective rate to approximately 8.0% for eligible manufacturing profits; no general tax holiday for dental aligner producers; scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) credits may apply to aligner material R&D (federal 15% ITC; Quebec 30% refundable credit for CEE in certain cases).
